tasks.short: Interview recipients at set intervals and certify continuing benefits.

steps.what: Interview benefits recipients at specified intervals

outputs: filed copy of signed continuing certification v1

tasks.design: The interviewer meets benefits recipients at the specified interval and certifies continuing eligibility. A job files that certification in {GOV_PORTAL} only after it is signed. Nothing renews a benefit on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Renewal could follow a date rather than a fresh certification.
tasks.enabler_now: The case record can store a signed certification.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer certifies or refuses continuing benefits.
tasks.altitude: The interview and the certification do not shrink. Filing the signed certification does.

reach.task: Continue pay only while the signed certification is in force

evidence.claim: Digest [S11] bars a solely automated decision with legal effect, so the interviewer authorizes every grant, denial, change, or amount.
Digest [S15] lists benefit eligibility as a high-risk use, and digest [S16] places those duties from 2 December 2027, so eligibility status stays with the interviewer.
Digest [S20] prohibits emotion recognition, so an interview is not scored for how a person sounds or looks.

assumptions: A date in the calendar is not a certification.
unknowns: How long a certification stays valid.
Who else must sign a refusal.
research_questions: How often recipients miss the interval interview.

already_counted.description: The interval interview and the certification stay inside the remaining time of those steps.

incremental.description: Update the published table or the required-field list when the rule changes, and clear cases the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only a completeness check or filing moves to a job. The interview, the decision, and the signature stay with the interviewer, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain eligibility, payment methods, and applicants' legal rights.

steps.what: Explain eligibility requirements and applicants' legal rights
Show published payment methods and application details
Interpret the information for this applicant

outputs: filed copy of signed explanation note v1

tasks.design: An answer desk shows the interviewer the published payment methods and application details in {DOCS}. The interviewer explains eligibility requirements and legal rights, interprets them for this applicant, and signs a note. The desk does not speak to the applicant and does not decide the case.
tasks.previous_blocker: The published text and the explanation were easy to mix, so a person could hear a rule that had changed.
tasks.enabler_now: Published pages can be shown from the maintained text.
tasks.still_hard: What this applicant needs to understand is still a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer interprets the rule and is responsible for what was said.
tasks.altitude: The explanation stays. Finding the published page and filing the note shrink.

reach.task: Ask again if the explanation is unclear
reach.learn: That the desk is not the decision

evidence.claim: The clerk digest says a model may draft a reply from the case record and the clerk sends it.
Digest [S11] bars a solely automated decision with legal effect, so the interviewer authorizes every grant, denial, change, or amount.

assumptions: The desk shows maintained text and does not draft a refusal.
The interviewer speaks to the applicant.
unknowns: Which text is the current published rule.
Whether a written explanation must follow the talk.
research_questions: How often the published text is behind the rule in force.

already_counted.description: Explaining and interpreting stay inside the remaining time of those steps.

incremental.description: Update the published table or the required-field list when the rule changes, and clear cases the job cannot file.

tasks.short: Grant, modify, deny, or terminate assistance, or refer to another agency.

steps.what: Initiate procedures to grant, modify, deny, or terminate
Refer applicants to other agencies for assistance
Draft the decision letter from the case record

loop.purpose: Draft the letter from the decision already written
loop.input: the interviewer's outcome notes and cited case rows
loop.check: every fact matches a case row and the outcome the interviewer wrote
loop.stop: one draft, or stop when a fact is not in the notes
loop.why_not_simpler: the letter wording changes with the outcome, so a single fixed paragraph does not fit

steps.what: Sign the assistance decision and letter

outputs: filed copy of signed assistance decision v1

tasks.design: The interviewer initiates the procedure to grant, modify, deny, or terminate, and refers applicants to other agencies when that is the outcome. A bounded draft in {DOCS} may phrase a letter only from that outcome and the case rows. The interviewer signs the decision and the letter, and a job sends that version. The draft is not the decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Letters were typed after a verbal outcome, and the version sent could differ from the decision.
tasks.enabler_now: A letter can be drafted from notes the interviewer already wrote.
tasks.still_hard: The outcome itself cannot be delegated.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer decides the outcome and what is sent.
tasks.altitude: The decision stays. Phrasing the letter and sending the signed version shrink.

reach.task: Act on the signed referral only

evidence.claim: Digest [S11] bars a solely automated decision with legal effect, so the interviewer authorizes every grant, denial, change, or amount.
Digest [S15] lists benefit eligibility as a high-risk use, and digest [S16] places those duties from 2 December 2027, so eligibility status stays with the interviewer.
The clerk digest says a model may draft a reply from the case record and the clerk sends it.
Digest [S13] says a score a decision-maker draws strongly on counts as the decision, so this design uses a published table and does not produce a score.

assumptions: The draft cannot change the outcome.
A changed outcome needs a new signature before send.
unknowns: Which outcomes require a second signature.
research_questions: How often the case rows are too thin for a letter.

already_counted.description: The grant, denial, change, or referral stays inside the remaining time of those steps.

tasks.short: Check employers or references to verify answers.

steps.what: Check with employers or other references
Verify answers and obtain further information

outputs: filed copy of signed verification note v1

tasks.design: The interviewer checks with employers or other references and verifies the answers. A job files the note in {GOV_PORTAL} only after the interviewer signs it. No job calls an employer or treats a mismatch as a decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verification calls were hard to trace back to the answer they checked.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed note can sit on the case file.
tasks.still_hard: What the reference said still has to be heard and judged.
tasks.human_edge: The interviewer decides whether the answer is verified.
tasks.altitude: The calls do not shrink. Filing the signed note does.

reach.task: Confirm only what they told the interviewer
reach.learn: That a job will not call them

evidence.claim: Digest [S11] bars a solely automated decision with legal effect, so the interviewer authorizes every grant, denial, change, or amount.
Digest [S21] says call recording and staff dashboards need works-council consent, so interviews are not recorded into a dashboard.

assumptions: The call stays with the interviewer.
A mismatch is not an automated denial.
unknowns: What consent the applicant gave for the check.
research_questions: How often references do not answer.

already_counted.description: The checks stay inside the remaining time of those steps.

role.altitude: The eligibility interviewer spends the week on the interview and the decision. Completeness checks and filing a signed note move to a job. No model decides a benefit or scores a person.
reach: Applicants hear the decision from the interviewer, not from a generated refusal.
Social workers receive only the extract the interviewer signed.
skills_to_grow: Tell a published table amount from the decision to authorize it.
Refuse any list that ranks or flags people.
role.ambitious_version: A signed decision can open the payment instruction, and the interviewer still authorizes that amount.
